summary: Fixed saturated orbit depth visualization by changing PNG/MP4 depth colorization bounds from raw finite min/max to robust per-setting percentile clipping by default, with explicit min/max override options. Raw metric depth .npy files remain saved directly from depth_to_meters without visualization clipping or normalization.
work_completed: Root cause: stable per-setting finite min/max still lets very large finite far-plane values or outliers dominate the range, compressing useful near-scene depths into a tiny viridis interval and making frames appear nearly single-color.

Added default 1st/99th percentile depth visualization bounds, sampled across saved per-setting .npy depth frames, plus CLI options for lower/upper percentiles, explicit min/max meters, and max samples.
Kept exact raw metric .npy output unchanged; clipping is only applied when generating viridis PNG frames and depth MP4 videos.
Updated flashlight orbit collection docs to describe percentile clipping, explicit visualization bounds, and raw .npy preservation.
Added focused tests for default options, invalid depth visualization args, outlier clipping contrast, and explicit bound overrides.

Validation passed: python -m py_compile examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py tests/test_orbit_collection_validation.py; python -m unittest tests.test_orbit_collection_validation ran 13 tests OK; helper smoke produced bounds (1.0, 4.0) and visualization [[0, 85, 170, 255, 255]] for a far-outlier depth sample; git diff --check passed.

findings.message: Depth visualization now clips finite metric depth samples to 1st/99th percentile by default, preventing huge finite depth values from flattening viridis contrast.
No Git commit or write outside the assigned product/docs/tests scope was performed.
Live SPEAR simulator validation was intentionally not run per task constraints; validation was limited to non-simulator tests and helper smoke checks.

follow_up_recommendations: Run one live orbit render in SPEAR when a simulator is available to visually confirm the default 1st/99th percentile bounds on real scene footage.
Review whether the default 1st/99th clipping should be tightened or loosened after inspecting representative orbit videos.
memory_worthy: Orbit collection depth PNG/MP4 visualization defaults to per-setting 1st/99th percentile clipping while preserving raw metric depth .npy outputs unchanged.
